title: Méry de Vic to Henri IV, 28 August 1589 (Dupuy 61 — Méry de Vic, f43r)

steps.what: George Lasry (with ChatGPT Astra 6 and Anthropic Opus 5.5) transcribed and deciphered the item: 6/6 pages transcribed; Partly deciphered; 545 elements, 523 identified (96.0%). Report section: Ciphertext-only.

Spot-check against the Gallica image (https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b103164206/f95.item): f43r: cleartext opening (Pompadour, Clermont Vertillac) + cipher block match his description; clear words between cipher runs read "...= roy q2 change come on ma asseure ... assemble aussi" whereas his excerpt gives "s est declare comme plusieurs du ? m ont asseure"; symbol-level decode not completed Verdict: partly confirmed.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): only George Lasry's report excerpt (lasry_entry.md) is in the repository; his full transcription and decryption are not, so they are recorded as missing (needs contributor: George Lasry).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): lasry_entry.md read; both excerpts have holes in every sentence (C confirmed) and the report says partly deciphered. Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read; method -> not solved; fraction_read 0.96 -> 0.

Gallica btv1b103164206 views 85-100 fetched through openapi.bnf.fr IIIF; the letter is ff. 40r-43r, clear except a 16-line cipher block on f. 43r (view 95); no decipherment or gloss on it or the neighbouring folios; no DECODE record. The block read sign by sign against Lasry's key table (texts/f43r_cipher_decode.tsv).

Decode compared with Lasry's two excerpts: both reproduced word for word where he has words; the 13 Oct spot-check disagreement is two different passages (l. B 's'est declare come plusieurs ... m'ont asseure', l. I clear 'se change come on ma asseure'). No key value adopted; sense-only ꝗ = g (ligue) and Ӿ = le(s) flagged for review.

Partial reading texts/f43r_reading.md (+ _en.md, log f43r_reread_log.md); b17_score.py (fr): body with clear text 0.667 (20/30), cipher passage alone 0.308 (4/13), explicit holes 0.462; 7 letters on look-alike alternates. Kept decoded, not read; blocker no-key-material for ~12 groups and 4 signs.

George Lasry's permission of 24 Oct 2026 covers his decryptions on DECODE. Searched the full DECODE record list (10,606 records, fetched 24 Oct 2026 with the project cookie) for this shelfmark (Dupuy 61 — Méry de Vic, f43r): no record, so DECODE holds no decryption of it; his full text exists only in his BnF cipher research report files. The excerpt state is kept.

George Lasry's report PDF (24 Oct 2026) received and extracted to lasry/report/ (summary, key image, excerpt and translation, full Readable text by folio); outcome.texts now points at his full text. Read share 0.998 (whole), 0.826 (deciphered passages); state read in part.

texts.label: George Lasry's decipherment (report PDF, 24 Oct 2026)
texts.summary: Méry de Vic writes after the assassination of Henri III and the accession of Henri IV. The opening cleartext reports the arrival of the news and local allegiances. The cipher reports troops near Limoges and divided loyalties; later cleartext discusses expenses, elections, intercepted dispatches and cannon for rebel forts.
texts.note: George Lasry's report PDF (24 Oct 2026), extracted to lasry/report/ (lasry_pdf_extract.py): his full Readable text by folio is the reading; he gives a translation of the excerpt only (lasry/report/translation_excerpt.md), no full translation. Report status: 6/6 pages transcribed; Partly deciphered. Measured 24 Oct 2026: whole text 0.998 (v10_relabel.measure, 2117 words); deciphered passages alone 0.826 (133 words, 16 unread groups, 10 doubtful words; a bare ? counted as unread). The whole letter passes the 95% bar only because it is mostly clear text; the cipher block on f43r alone does not (four signs and about twelve groups without a value in his key), so read in part. State: read in part.
